sections.heading: How to convert a PDF to text
sections.body:
Open the [PDF to text converter](https://pdf-to-text.lazur.app/converter) in your browser. The steps are short.

1. Choose your PDF, or drop the file into the box. The limit is 15 MB.
2. Wait a few seconds while the file is read. Most files finish in about 1 to 3 seconds.
3. Read the text on the screen and check it against the PDF.
4. Copy the text with one click and paste it into a note, an email or a document.

The converter gives you plain text. It does not rebuild the page, so you paste the words into the app where you want to keep them. Start with a short PDF, such as one page, to see the result before you convert a long file.

sections.heading: Two kinds of PDF
sections.body:
A PDF made from a Word file, a web page or a report usually has real text in it. A PDF made by scanning a paper page usually does not. The converter handles both, but the scanned kind needs more checking.

For a text PDF, the output should match the page closely. Names, dates and numbers are usually exact, and headings stay in order. For a scanned PDF, the tool reads the words from the picture of each page. Clear print works well. Faded copies, handwriting and tiny footnotes can come out wrong, so compare those lines with the original before you use them.

**Try a selection first.** Drag your mouse across a line in the PDF viewer. If the words highlight, the file already has text, and the converter is only copying it out.

sections.heading: What the output keeps and drops
sections.body:
The result is the text in reading order. Paragraphs stay as paragraphs, and headings stay where they were on the page. Nothing is added before or after the text, so you do not get a summary or a comment from the tool.

The output does not keep fonts, colors, images, page numbers placed in boxes or the layout of columns. If a page has several columns, the text may come out in an order you did not expect. Read those pages once against the PDF, and move any lines that landed in the wrong place.

sections.heading: Checking the result
sections.body:
Before you use the text, read three places: the first lines, the numbers and the last lines. The first lines tell you whether the reading order is right. The numbers are where a small misread matters most, such as a 3 that became an 8 in a scanned page. The last lines show whether the file was read to the end.

If a page looks wrong, convert that page again on its own. A cleaner scan often gives a better result than a large file with many pages in one go.

For the free runs, you get 3 a day. Leave an email and you get 3 more that day. You do not need an account. The PDF is sent to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini reads it, so do not send a file you are not allowed to share with an online service.

faq.q: Can the converter read a scanned PDF?
faq.a: Yes. For a scanned PDF, the tool reads the text from the picture of each page. Clear, printed pages give the best result. Check names, numbers and small print against the original, because scans with blur or handwriting can come out wrong.

faq.q: What is the file size limit?
faq.a: A PDF can be up to 15 MB. Larger files are not accepted. If your PDF is over the limit, split it into smaller files, convert each part, and paste the parts together in order.

faq.a: No. The output is plain text in reading order, with paragraphs and headings kept. Fonts, colors, images and column layout are not kept, so paste the text into the app where you want to format it.

sections.heading: Why plain text helps an AI chat
sections.body:
An AI chat works with the words you give it. When you paste the text of a PDF, the model gets the wording, the headings and the order of the paragraphs. It does not get the page design, the images or the fonts, and it does not need them for most tasks such as summarizing, finding a clause or answering a question.

That is why a clean text copy is often the best input. The PDF itself can be large, and some chats limit what they accept from a file upload. Plain text is light, and you can see exactly what you are sending.

sections.heading: Steps: from PDF to AI chat
sections.body:
1. Open the [PDF to text for AI](https://pdf-to-text.lazur.app/ai) page and choose your PDF. The file can be up to 15 MB.
2. Wait a few seconds while the tool reads it. Most files finish in about 1 to 3 seconds.
3. Read the output against the PDF, especially the numbers and names.
4. Copy the text with one click.
5. Open your AI chat, paste the text, and add your question before or after it.

Keep your question short and specific. For example, ask for the three main points, or ask where the document mentions a date. A clear question gets a clear answer from the text you pasted.

If the text is long, ask about one part at a time. Paste the section you need and name its heading, so the answer points back to the right place in the PDF when you check it.

sections.heading: Check the text before you trust the answer
sections.body:
The AI can only work with the text it receives. If the conversion misread a number or dropped a line, the answer will repeat that mistake with confidence. Compare any figure you plan to use with the PDF.

Scanned PDFs need the most checking. The tool reads the words from the picture of each page, so clear, printed pages are safest. Faded pages, handwriting and very small print can come out wrong. Tables and multi-column pages can come out in an order you did not expect, so read those sections against the original before you ask about them.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
sections.body:
You get 3 free runs a day. Leave an email and you get 3 more runs that day. You do not need an account for either.

The PDF is sent to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini reads it and sends back the text. If the PDF holds private or confidential material, check your rules before you upload it, and do not paste text into a chat you are not allowed to use for that material.

faq.q: Can I turn a PDF into text for an AI?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the PDF to this tool, copy the text it returns, and paste that text into your AI chat. The output is plain text in reading order, so the AI gets the wording and the order of the document.

faq.q: Can AI convert a PDF to text?

faq.q: Do I need to clean the text before pasting it into an AI?
faq.a: Usually not. Read the first lines, the numbers and the last lines against the PDF to make sure the text is in order. Fix any line that is out of place, then paste. Long copies may need to be split into parts if your AI chat limits the input size.

pages.description: Convert a PDF to text on your Mac with a free browser tool, or copy text in Preview with Tools, Text Selection. Steps for scanned PDFs too.
pages.claim: On a Mac, open this tool in your browser, upload the PDF, and copy the text. For a PDF with selectable text, Preview can also copy it: choose Tools, Text Selection, then Edit, Copy. Free, no account.

sections.heading: Option 1: the browser tool on your Mac
sections.body:
This works for any PDF, including scans, because the tool reads the text itself. You need a browser and a PDF on your Mac.

1. Open the [PDF to text tool for Mac](https://pdf-to-text.lazur.app/mac) in your browser.
2. Choose your PDF from your Mac, or drop it into the box. The file can be up to 15 MB.
3. Wait a few seconds while the file is read.
4. Copy the result with one click and paste it into a note, email or document.

You can run it 3 times a day for free without an account. Leave an email and you get 3 more runs that day.

sections.heading: Option 2: copy text in Preview
sections.body:
Preview is the PDF viewer that comes with macOS. If the PDF already has text in it, you can copy that text without any upload. Apple's guide to Preview describes the steps.

1. Open the PDF in Preview.
2. Choose Tools, then Text Selection.
3. Drag across the text you want.
4. Choose Edit, then Copy.
5. Paste the text where you need it.

To copy a column from a table, hold the Option key while you drag, then choose Edit, then Copy. The steps are in [Apple's Preview guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/preview/prvw1020/mac).

sections.heading: When Preview will not copy
sections.body:
If the Text Selection tool does not pick up any words, the PDF is probably a scan. A scan is a picture of a page, so Preview has no text to copy. Use the browser tool above for that file.

Other causes are a password on the PDF, which Preview asks for, or a copy lock set by whoever made the file. Check the Text Selection setting under Tools first, because it can be switched off. If nothing works, use the browser tool, which reads the text from the picture of each page.

sections.heading: Check the text, then decide
sections.body:
Whichever option you use, check the copied text against the PDF. Read the first lines, the numbers and the last lines. A copy from Preview keeps the words exactly as they are in the file, so the risk is in scans, where the browser tool reads the picture and can misread small print.

Preview gives you the words only, not the page design, images or fonts. Paste into a plain text editor if you want to see exactly what you have.

If you write a lot from notes you read in PDFs, Lazur can help with the typing: hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in on your Mac.

faq.q: How do I convert a PDF to text on a Mac?
faq.a: You have two free options. Open the PDF in Preview and copy its text with Tools, Text Selection, then Edit, Copy. Or open the PDF to text tool in your browser, upload the PDF, and copy the result. Preview only works when the PDF already has text in it.

faq.q: Can I copy text from a PDF on a Mac without an app?
faq.a: Yes. Open the PDF to text tool in your browser on your Mac, upload the file, and copy the text with one click. No install and no account are needed. You get 3 free runs a day.

faq.q: Why can't I select text in my PDF on a Mac?
faq.a: The PDF is probably a scan, which is a picture of a page with no text in it. It can also have a copy lock or a password. Try the PDF to text tool, which reads the text from the image. For a password, open the file in Preview and enter it first.
